# 04 · Order: cancelling a fulfillment puts the order back to unfulfilled

**Type:** Test coverage · **Area:** Orders / Fulfillment · **Priority:** Medium

## Context

Warehouse staff sometimes fulfil an order by mistake, or a parcel is never collected. They then
cancel the fulfillment from the fulfillment card's menu, choosing the warehouse the stock goes
back to. We cover fulfilling (`order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts`) but not cancelling one.

## What to cover

1. Open the paid and fulfilled order from the orders test data.
2. Cancel its fulfillment, returning the stock to a warehouse.
3. The order goes back to needing fulfillment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After confirming, the order's status reads "Unfulfilled".
- [ ] The order offers the fulfil action again.
- [ ] The order is still "Unfulfilled" after the page is reloaded.

## Notes

- The orders test data already has a paid, fulfilled order.
- The cancel dialog asks for a warehouse; any warehouse it offers is fine.

105	By default the database is restored **before every test**, and those tests run one at a
106	time. That single property is what the suite is for: a failing test reproduces on its own,
107	rather than as a function of the tests that ran before it. Specs need no cleanup
108	discipline and no unique names, and nothing in the seed is ever consumed.
109	
110	Serial is the default because a restore empties every table for a second or two — a test
111	running alongside one would see a shop with no products and no users in it.
112	
113	A block that leaves nothing behind can opt out of the reset, and then run in parallel:
114	
115	```ts
116	import { parallel } from "../config.ts";
117	
118	test.describe("Catalogue list", { tag: parallel() }, () => { ... });      // default scenario
119	test.describe("Refunds", { tag: parallel("refunded-orders") }, () => { ... });
120	```
121	
122	The tag takes a **scenario name**, so the group and the database state it runs on are the
123	same thing and cannot drift apart. A run is then:
124	
125	```
126	restore:default          one restore, alone
127	parallel:default         every test tagged parallel(),          all at once
128	restore:refunded-orders  one restore, alone
129	parallel:refunded-orders every test tagged parallel("refunded-orders"), all at once
130	stable                   everything untagged, one at a time, each from its own reset
131	```
132	
133	Groups run one after another and all of them before the serial phase, rather than
134	interleaved in declaration order. That is deliberate, and it is also the cheaper
135	arrangement: this costs one restore per group plus one per serial test, where interleaving
136	would add a restore at every boundary and buy nothing — tests are independent by
137	construction, so the order between groups carries no meaning.
138	
139	Playwright's project `dependencies` are what enforce it; they are the only ordering
140	primitive that spans workers, which is also why a group's restore is a project rather than
141	a hook. A scenario with no tagged tests still pays for its restore project (a second or
142	two) — whether a group has members is not knowable when the config is read.
143	
144	`E2E_WORKERS` (default 4) sets how wide the parallel phase runs. Each test is a browser
145	context, so the ceiling is memory rather than cores.
146	
147	Because arrangement cannot be done as an admin at test time, **a state a spec needs is a
148	scenario**, named and built, not something the spec creates on the way past.
149	
150	### What cannot be tagged: signing in

153	concurrent requests" (`saleor/account/throttling.py`), unconditionally in `tokenCreate`,
154	with no setting to disable it. Every test here comes from the same address, so parallel

input.name: Order: cancelling a fulfillment puts the order back to unfulfilled
input.overview:
Ticket 04. Warehouse staff cancel a fulfillment from the fulfillment card's "Show more" menu on the order details page, picking the warehouse the stock is restocked to. Afterwards the order goes back to needing fulfillment: the status pill reads "Unfulfilled", the "Fulfill" action is offered again, and both survive a page reload. Fulfilling is already covered by e2e/tests/orders/order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts. Cancelling is not.

Target test file: e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel-fulfillment.spec.ts
Seed file used for exploration: e2e/tests/seed.spec.ts (suite fixture e2e/fixtures/test.ts: restored DB plus signed-in admin, dashboard at http://localhost:9200).

Test data and setup (follow the existing order specs):
- The seed restores the "default" scenario, which does NOT contain the scenario orders. The spec must declare `test.use({ scenario: ORDERS_SCENARIO })` (from e2e/scenarios/orders.ts) so the fixture restores the "orders" dump before the test.
- The order is the scenario order keyed "fulfilled" (SCENARIO_ORDERS.fulfilled): one "E2E Tee", paid with orderMarkAsPaid, fulfilled with one fulfillment from the warehouse that ships to US in default-channel (Channel-USD). It is tagged with metadata e2e=fulfilled. Order ids change with every dump build, so look the id up at test time with `await findOrderId(e2eConfig(), "fulfilled")` and open it with `OrderPage.goto(id)`, which waits for the status pill.
- Leave the test untagged (serial, with its own DB reset), because it mutates the order. Do not use parallel(). Tag the title with "#e2e", the same as the sibling order specs.
- Follow the Arrange / Act / Assert comments and test.step() style used in order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts.

Confirmed UI flow and selectors (seen on a populatedb fulfilled order, same components):
- Status pill: getByTestId("status-info") (OrderPage.statusInfo). Reads "Fulfilled" before and "Unfulfilled" after.
- The order lines card opens in the "Line matrix" view in a fresh browser context, and that view has no fulfillment card. Switch to "Timeline" first: getByTestId("order-items-view-timeline") (OrderPage.timelineView). The choice persists in browser storage across reloads, but each test starts from a fresh context.
- Fulfillment card: getByTestId("fulfilled-order-section"). Its header shows the date, "From <warehouse>", "Fulfilled", "Add tracking", and a "Show more" icon button getByTestId("fulfillment-menu-button").
- Menu item: role menuitem "Cancel fulfillment", data-test-id "cancel-fulfillment". The same test id is also used in OrderLineExpandedPanel (Line matrix view), so scope it with getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Cancel fulfillment" }) or getByRole("menu").getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment").
- Clicking it adds ?action=cancel-fulfillment&id=<fulfillmentId> to the URL and opens a dialog (getByRole("dialog"), OrderPage.dialog) titled "Cancel Fulfillment". Body text: "...Canceling a fulfillment will restock products at the selected warehouse. The warehouse this fulfillment shipped from is pre-selected."
- Warehouse field: wrapper getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment-select-field"), containing combobox "Select Warehouse". The fulfillment's source warehouse is pre-selected, and the submit button is enabled straight away. Opening the combobox shows a listbox of role option / data-test-id "select-option" with every warehouse (populatedb: Oceania, Europe, Default Warehouse, Default for click and collect, Default, Asia, Americas, Africa). The ticket accepts any warehouse.
- Buttons: dialog getByTestId("back") ("Back"), getByTestId("close-button") (X), and getByTestId("submit") ("Cancel fulfillment").
- On success the dialog closes, a toast shows "Success / Fulfillment cancelled", the status pill reads "Unfulfilled", the "Fulfill" button getByTestId("order-items-fulfill-button") (OrderPage.fulfillButton) appears in both views, the lines card shows "Unfulfilled order lines" plus a "Show 1 canceled shipment" button, and Order History adds "Fulfillment was cancelled" and "Restocked 1 item to <warehouse>".

Page-object reuse and suggested additions (e2e/pages/orderPage.ts):
- Reuse: goto(orderId), statusInfo, fulfillButton, timelineView, dialog.
- Add locators: fulfillmentMenuButton = getByTestId("fulfillment-menu-button"), cancelFulfillmentMenuItem = getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Cancel fulfillment" }), cancelFulfillmentWarehouse = dialog.getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment-select-field").getByRole("combobox").
- Add a helper `cancelFulfillment(warehouse?: string)`: click timelineView, click fulfillmentMenuButton, click cancelFulfillmentMenuItem, optionally open the combobox and pick getByRole("option", { name: warehouse, exact: true }), click dialog.getByTestId("submit"), then wait for the dialog to be hidden. # Order: cancelling a fulfillment puts the order back to unfulfilled

## Application Overview

Ticket 04. Warehouse staff cancel a fulfillment from the fulfillment card's "Show more" menu on the order details page, picking the warehouse the stock is restocked to. Afterwards the order goes back to needing fulfillment: the status pill reads "Unfulfilled", the "Fulfill" action is offered again, and both survive a page reload. Fulfilling is already covered by e2e/tests/orders/order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts. Cancelling is not.

Target test file: e2e/tests/orders/order-cancel-fulfillment.spec.ts
Seed file used for exploration: e2e/tests/seed.spec.ts (suite fixture e2e/fixtures/test.ts: restored DB plus signed-in admin, dashboard at http://localhost:9200).

Test data and setup (follow the existing order specs):
- The seed restores the "default" scenario, which does NOT contain the scenario orders. The spec must declare `test.use({ scenario: ORDERS_SCENARIO })` (from e2e/scenarios/orders.ts) so the fixture restores the "orders" dump before the test.
- The order is the scenario order keyed "fulfilled" (SCENARIO_ORDERS.fulfilled): one "E2E Tee", paid with orderMarkAsPaid, fulfilled with one fulfillment from the warehouse that ships to US in default-channel (Channel-USD). It is tagged with metadata e2e=fulfilled. Order ids change with every dump build, so look the id up at test time with `await findOrderId(e2eConfig(), "fulfilled")` and open it with `OrderPage.goto(id)`, which waits for the status pill.
- Leave the test untagged (serial, with its own DB reset), because it mutates the order. Do not use parallel(). Tag the title with "#e2e", the same as the sibling order specs.
- Follow the Arrange / Act / Assert comments and test.step() style used in order-payment-fulfillment.spec.ts.

Confirmed UI flow and selectors (seen on a populatedb fulfilled order, same components):
- Status pill: getByTestId("status-info") (OrderPage.statusInfo). Reads "Fulfilled" before and "Unfulfilled" after.
- The order lines card opens in the "Line matrix" view in a fresh browser context, and that view has no fulfillment card. Switch to "Timeline" first: getByTestId("order-items-view-timeline") (OrderPage.timelineView). The choice persists in browser storage across reloads, but each test starts from a fresh context.
- Fulfillment card: getByTestId("fulfilled-order-section"). Its header shows the date, "From <warehouse>", "Fulfilled", "Add tracking", and a "Show more" icon button getByTestId("fulfillment-menu-button").
- Menu item: role menuitem "Cancel fulfillment", data-test-id "cancel-fulfillment". The same test id is also used in OrderLineExpandedPanel (Line matrix view), so scope it with getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Cancel fulfillment" }) or getByRole("menu").getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment").
- Clicking it adds ?action=cancel-fulfillment&id=<fulfillmentId> to the URL and opens a dialog (getByRole("dialog"), OrderPage.dialog) titled "Cancel Fulfillment". Body text: "...Canceling a fulfillment will restock products at the selected warehouse. The warehouse this fulfillment shipped from is pre-selected."
- Warehouse field: wrapper getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment-select-field"), containing combobox "Select Warehouse". The fulfillment's source warehouse is pre-selected, and the submit button is enabled straight away. Opening the combobox shows a listbox of role option / data-test-id "select-option" with every warehouse (populatedb: Oceania, Europe, Default Warehouse, Default for click and collect, Default, Asia, Americas, Africa). The ticket accepts any warehouse.
- Buttons: dialog getByTestId("back") ("Back"), getByTestId("close-button") (X), and getByTestId("submit") ("Cancel fulfillment").
- On success the dialog closes, a toast shows "Success / Fulfillment cancelled", the status pill reads "Unfulfilled", the "Fulfill" button getByTestId("order-items-fulfill-button") (OrderPage.fulfillButton) appears in both views, the lines card shows "Unfulfilled order lines" plus a "Show 1 canceled shipment" button, and Order History adds "Fulfillment was cancelled" and "Restocked 1 item to <warehouse>".

Page-object reuse and suggested additions (e2e/pages/orderPage.ts):
- Reuse: goto(orderId), statusInfo, fulfillButton, timelineView, dialog.
- Add locators: fulfillmentMenuButton = getByTestId("fulfillment-menu-button"), cancelFulfillmentMenuItem = getByRole("menuitem", { name: "Cancel fulfillment" }), cancelFulfillmentWarehouse = dialog.getByTestId("cancel-fulfillment-select-field").getByRole("combobox").
- Add a helper `cancelFulfillment(warehouse?: string)`: click timelineView, click fulfillmentMenuButton, click cancelFulfillmentMenuItem, optionally open the combobox and pick getByRole("option", { name: warehouse, exact: true }), click dialog.getByTestId("submit"), then wait for the dialog to be hidden.     - expect: getByTestId("status-info") has text exactly "Unfulfilled" (acceptance criterion 1)
    - expect: getByTestId("order-items-fulfill-button") is visible with text "Fulfill" (acceptance criterion 2)

await page.goto('http://localhost:9200/orders/');


### Find a fulfilled order id for exploration
```ts
await page.evaluate('async () => { const api=\'http://localhost:8200/graphql/\'; const r=await fetch(api,{method:\'POST\',headers:{\'content-type\':\'application/json\'},body:JSON.stringify({query:\'mutation($t:String){tokenRefresh(refreshToken:$t){token}}\',variables:{t:localStorage.getItem(\'_saleorRefreshToken\')}})}).then(r=>r.json()); const token=r.data.tokenRefresh.token; const o=await fetch(api,{method:\'POST\',headers:{\'content-type\':\'application/json\',authorization:\'Bearer \'+token},body:JSON.stringify({query:\'{orders(first:5, filter:{status:[FULFILLED]}){edges{node{id number status}}}}\'})}).then(r=>r.json()); return o; }');
```
